item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD with diagonals AC and BD meeting at O. Kavya measures $AC = BD$, $AO = OC$, and $BO = OD$.

Which claim about ABCD is correct?

options.A: ABCD is a rectangle, because its diagonals are equal and bisect each other.
options.B: ABCD is a rectangle from $AC = BD$ alone.
options.C: The rectangle name is what creates equal bisecting diagonals, so the measurements cannot start the claim.
options.D: The same measurements also make any two equal crossing sticks on the desk a rectangle.
